title: DC-area forecast: Slowly warmer into Friday. On the edge of a coastal storm this weekend.
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: A pause in the gusty breeze as evening 50s drop to overnight lows in the upper 40s to low 50s.

What’s next? Around or above 70 Friday with more sun around. Some questions remain about an offshore storm this weekend, but we should stay on the edge of it at worst.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Partly cloudy skies have enough clearing for lows to fall farther than recent nights, reaching the upper 40s to low 50s. Winds are from the north around 5 to 10 mph. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Friday): Looking pretty nice, if also on the breezy side. A coastal low well offshore helps crank up our winds from the north to around 15 mph, with gusts near 25 to 30 mph. But skies should be mainly sunny, with highs ending up around 70 or into the low 70s. Confidence: Medium-High

Tomorrow night: Partly to mostly clear and still breezy. Temperatures fall to lows in the 50s. Confidence: Medium-High

A look ahead

For the weekend, models are struggling with the track of a big storm off the coast. Some bring it close enough to push showers into our area, especially later Saturday into Sunday from near DC and I-95 to the east. Highs look like the upper 60s to low 70s Saturday with partly sunny skies, and mid- to upper 60s Sunday with partly to mostly cloudy skies, as winds gust up to near 30 mph. Confidence: Low-Medium

The meandering coastal low should be moving away more decisively by Monday, meaning diminishing breezes and increasing sunshine. Warmer temperatures also become more likely, with highs around the mid-70s. Confidence: Medium

College Park tornado

A powerful 2001 tornado struck College Park, killing two and injuring dozens, while in 2010 extreme late-season heat pushed temperatures to a record 99 degrees.

Today’s daily digit — 6/10: Partial sunshine feels like a big win after several days dominated by rain and clouds. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.
